newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Esso to deploy 2 Bass Strait platforms.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Esso to deploy 2 Bass Strait platforms.

text.p: Esso Australia Ltd will early next week begin towing its largest Australian offshore oil and gas platform, West Tuna, to Bass Strait where it will stand as the centrepiece of the now declining oil field.

The 100,000-tonne West Tuna will be deployed 56 km off southeast Australia as part of the joint venture Bass Strait operations owned equally by The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and operator Esso, a wholly owned unit of Exxon Corp.
A smaller platform, Bream B, will be towed to Bass Strait a month later to compliment Bream A, currently extracting oil and gas from the Bream field some 33 km offshore.

The two platforms, built at a total cost of A$1.1 billion, mark a technological first for Australia with the use of steel-reinforced concrete gravity structures taking the place of traditional steel jackets, Esso officials told Reuters.

Esso said that in calendar 1997 the platforms were expected to add 30,000 barrels of crude oil and condensate per day (bpd) to total field production, which currently runs at between 205,000 and 210,000 bpd.
Production from Bass Strait, Australia's largest oil and gas field, has been declining steadily since 1985 when output peaked at about 500,000 barrels a day.
West Tuna, to begin production in February 1997, will be fed by 40 wells to be drilled over four years, Esso said.
The unmanned Bream B will be producing by December this year with a total 15 wells expected to be completed in November 1997.
By the time West Tuna's drilling is completed, the two facilities will be feeding a total of about 45,000 bpd into the pipelines leading to the Long Island Point processing and storage facility.

Esso corporate and public affairs manager Ron Webb said that while West Tuna and Bream B were unlikely to be the last of the Bass Strait platforms, the joint venture partners had not planned any additional platforms for the area in the near term.
"Near term we don't have any particular plans on the drawing board ... the big fields in Bass Strait have been found," Webb said.
